role: Extension of ReanalysisService: sleep retro-apply over all overnight sessions, manual-window reanalysis/apply, sleep-boundary updates (user edits and automatic HealthKit refreshes) with re-scoring, training-snapshot repair, and segment unlinking.

units.does: Filters sessions to overnight ones with RR data, re-runs the sleep pipeline for each (stopping on cancellation) counting rewritten sessions, reports progress, notifies archive changed, logs and returns the count.
For one session: end = endDate or start+12 h; fetches fresh sleep, checks shouldRetroApply, writes boundaries/segments/snapshot, re-scores, and persists; returns whether it was written.

flags.text: retroApply rewrites the full HRVSession copy that RRCollector.archivedSessions loaded at the start of the sweep, after an await on HealthKit per session, via archive.archive (whole-object write); any edit made to that session meanwhile (feeling, tags, sleep edit, score refresh) is overwritten. persistSnapshot in the same file re-reads from the archive for exactly this reason; retroApply does not.

units.does: Fetches HealthKit sleep for the session (validated against its RR points); nil on error (logged).

branches.effect: logged and swallowed; return nil so the session is skipped

flags.text: Retro-apply's sleep fetch omits the prior-day nap credit that every morning-path fetch adds (fetchDaytimeNapMinutes + withNapSleepMinutes), then replaces sleepSnapshot and re-scores, so applying sleep settings retroactively drops nap minutes from 24 h sleep and can lower past recovery scores.

units.does: Allows retro-apply only when the new sleep has night minutes or stage intervals, the session is not user-adjusted, and the sleep block plausibly overlaps start..sessionEnd.

branches.cond: no night minutes and no stage intervals

overwrite sleepEndMs; nil leaves the old value

flags.text: docs/FLOWCHART.md §13.1 lists updateSessionSleepBoundaries as a user-initiated path (trigger: timeline editor Done), but several callers invoke it automatically with the default isUserAdjustment false (RecordView+Sections.swift:349,401; HistoryView.swift:455; ImportDataView.swift:123), and those go through the 'more data' gate instead.

retrieve (one lock) then archive (a second lock) is not atomic: an edit landing between them is overwritten by the whole-session write. SessionArchive.update(_:requestingReupload:_:) exists to do read-modify-write under one lock for exactly this case.

units.does: Computes new start offset (>=0) and unclamped end offset, logs, applies the automatic-update gate unless user adjustment, writes boundaries, re-scores and persists; returns true when written.

flags.text: A sleep edit or automatic sleep update rewrites sleepSnapshot and re-scores with useBaselineHRV: !isReliableForHRVAggregates, but never re-classifies hrvDataQuality; .preSleep is decided from the sleep overlap (SessionAcceptanceService.swift:75-77), so a session flagged .preSleep stays flagged (baseline HRV substituted) even after the user's edit makes the recording overlap sleep.
